summary.headline: Jinkushal Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 89% YoY to INR133 crore, a record quarter, but full-year PAT was only INR12.44 crore as logistics and HexL brand costs weighed.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered the highest quarterly standalone and consolidated revenue in company history, with standalone revenue up 89% YoY to INR133 crore and consolidated at INR192 crore. Full-year standalone revenue grew 48% to INR313 crore, but standalone PAT was INR12.44 crore and consolidated PAT was INR12.76 crore, with management attributing the margin pressure to freight and geopolitical logistics costs, HexL brand investment and higher employee costs. Consolidated net worth rose from INR86 crore to INR194 crore after the IPO, while working capital increased on higher volumes and overseas inventory. Management declined to give FY27 revenue guidance, citing the Middle East conflict, and reiterated a medium-term target of INR600-700 crore revenue in 2.5-3 years.

segments.name: Product mix FY26 (consolidated revenue)
segments.commentary: Customised machines of other brands contributed about 62%, refurbished used construction equipment about 35%, and HexL own-brand about 5% (4.9-5% consolidated; about 7% standalone).

segments.name: Geography FY26
segments.commentary: Mexico about 46%, UAE about 19%, South Africa and Australia about 10% each (per management's approximate figures), with the rest in single digits. Management said exports are about 97-98% of revenue.

segments.name: HexL brand
segments.commentary: Own brand in early build-out with lower margins; management targets 11-12% of FY27 revenue and about 150 units in FY27.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 revenue growth guidance given, citing geopolitical uncertainty around the Middle East conflict and the Strait of Hormuz.
Medium-term vision of INR600-700 crore revenue in 2.5-3 years, reiterated from the prior call.
Medium-term targets: revenue of INR600-800 crore at about 5-7% consolidated PAT margin before focusing on cash conversion cycle.
Management expects FY27 profitability to improve faster than revenue if Middle East logistics normalise.
Long-run margin targets: 12-14% PAT for HexL and refurbished used equipment; 2-4% for new equipment of other brands.
HexL unit milestones to track: 100, 250 and 500 units; FY27 target about 150 units.
Cash conversion cycle expected to improve next year, not in the near term.
capex_capacity: Overseas inventory held above INR50 crore as at 31 March 2026; about 70% available for retail opportunities and 30% allocated to customers pending order confirmation.
Offices in Dubai and Kissimmee, Florida, USA.
Management said capital, not market size, is the main constraint on growth; refurbishment expertise is cited as the operating base.
No immediate plans for new overseas geographies or inventory hubs, though 80-100 countries are cited as the long-term addressable base.
Management did not disclose a new manufacturing unit or specific capex plan.
demand_pricing: Management said demand for construction and mining equipment stayed resilient, supported by infrastructure, industrial capex and replacement demand in emerging markets.
West Asia crisis raised logistics costs, freight, insurance and currency volatility; management said freight costs were absorbed in P&L and were the main reason for profit decline.
Mexico Q4 performance was better than Q3, but management did not quantify FY26 Mexico decline.
South Africa emerged as a strong contributor to offset moderation in other markets.
No order pipeline; inventory-led sales model with working capital churn of 2-2.5 times.
Management did not provide a figure for repeat-customer share, saying a large majority of orders are repeat orders.

qa_highlights.question: Will management guide FY27 revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is premature to give FY27 guidance given the geopolitical situation, but reiterated the INR600-700 crore revenue target in 2.5-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What are the medium-term targets for ROCE, cash conversion cycle and EBITDA margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management prioritised scale to INR600-800 crore revenue at about 5-7% consolidated PAT, and said cash conversion cycle would stay elevated while HexL is built.

qa_highlights.question: How will HexL affect working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory positioning and customer credit for HexL keep the cash conversion cycle higher; management expects it to ease after the brand is established, next year at the earliest.

qa_highlights.question: What share of FY26 revenue came from HexL and what are FY27 targets?
qa_highlights.answer: HexL was about 5% of consolidated FY26 revenue and about 7% of standalone; the FY27 target is 11-12% of revenue and about 150 units.

qa_highlights.question: What is the geographic mix and how is Mexico trending?
qa_highlights.answer: Mexico about 46%, UAE about 19%, South Africa and Australia about 10% each; management said Mexico Q4 was stronger than Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital requirement for further growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital is INR300-350 crore; management said each INR100 crore of additional working capital could support roughly INR200-300 crore of revenue after the INR600-700 crore milestone.

risks_watch: Freight, insurance and currency costs from the West Asia conflict, which management says drove the profit decline.
Working capital and cash conversion cycle, which management expects to stay elevated; operating cash flow lags revenue.
Concentration risk: Mexico (about 46%) and UAE (about 19%) of FY26 revenue.
HexL brand economics, with lower early margins and unit sales milestones of 100, 250 and 500 units to track.
Limited FY27 visibility, with no order pipeline and no guidance.
Transcript notes that the company is ~97-98% export-oriented and that FTA benefits are not yet visible in the numbers.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term scale and brand plans, but cautious and at times evasive on near-term numbers: management declined FY27 guidance, revenue visibility and turnover targets, citing geopolitical uncertainty.
key_quotes: We are particularly encouraged by the strong momentum witnessed during the fourth quarter, which resulted in the highest quarterly standalone and consolidated revenue in the company's history.
In the current geopolitical situation, I think it will be premature to give any revenue growth guidance immediately in the current few quarters.
And the only limiting factor would only be the capital available to the company, which it can utilize and grow its business.
I think the number of units being sold, I think that's the top indicator in any construction equipment or automotive sector.
